data.ruling: The refutation stands. The requirement list leaves out an owner decision that applies to this accelerometer. V206 (owner, 2026-09-28) answers "Yes, to 0.1°, 2 axes, zeroed on a reference surface". The list's "sensing axis" asks for at least one axis, which is weaker than V206's 2 axes. The list also gives no static, DC-coupled resolution: 0.1° is sin(0.1°) x 1 g = 1.75 mg. V206 is filed under R10 and says "an accelerometer on the surface". Even so, the project names one accelerometer. The specification says "the accelerometer" in IOBoard.md:454, docs/Servo.md:80 and shared/servo/include/servo_sync.h:24-25 ("a separate measurement with the accelerometer on the surface"). R10's kept converter (ADCS7476AIMFX/NOPB, FU-C1) is sized at 2 channels for "the 2 static-angle axes" of the ADXL316, R11's accelerometer. This task's own P2 "R11 pins" figure says "V206 adds a second [channel] for the static angle". A list that the function's part is qualified against must carry V206's 2 axes and 0.1° (1.75 mg) static resolution. The failure is about this function's requirements, not about a part. The verifier's note that ADXL316 (3 axes, DC response) is not refuted by this is not ruled on here.
data.evidence: Research.md:766 V206, "Must the converter for the accelerometer also measure a control surface's static angle from gravity, with an accelerometer on the surface, and if so to what resolution, in degrees?": "Yes, to 0.1°, 2 axes, zeroed on a reference surface (owner, 2026-09-28)". IOBoard.md:451 "one axis, across the shaft" (balance only). IOBoard.md:454: "Two servos that agree with each other and are both wrong need the accelerometer or inspection. An accelerometer on the control surface cannot observe rotation about the gravity vector". servo_sync.h:23-25: "That is a separate measurement with the accelerometer on the surface." FU-C1/003-P2-R10.json, R10 converter: "channels: 2 channels: the 2 static-angle axes, one of them the vibration axis"; "static angle resolution: 0.1 degree (1.75 mg at 1 g) on 2 axes, DC-coupled"; placements 2 "for the 2 axes of V206". selection.json R10 keeps ADCS7476AIMFX/NOPB (run FU-C1). The FU-C2 P2-R11 "R11 pins" figure: "The accelerometer takes 1 converter channel for the one in-plane axis (R10's V201; V206 adds a second for the static angle)". The P2-R11 accelerometer requirement list, re-read from scratch/FU-C2/P2-R11/out.json, has 11 entries matching the claim. It has no 2-axis entry and no static-angle entry: "sensing axis | at least one axis in the mounting plane".
